articles.headline: Man City charges: Premier League clubs seeking legal advice amid expected guilty verdicts
articles.description: Premier League clubs are seeking legal advice amid an expectation that Man City have been found guilty of hundreds of breaches of financial regulations, sources have told ESPN.
articles.body:
A number of Premier League clubs are seeking legal advice amid an expectation that Manchester City have been found guilty of hundreds of breaches of financial regulations, sources have told ESPN.

The decision of the independent panel which heard the Premier League's case against City has not been formally communicated.

However, a source has told ESPN that they've been made aware that a decision has been reached after deliberations which lasted 22 months.

City are refusing to deny that they've been informed that a guilty verdict has been handed down in the majority of the 115 charges which have formed the Premier League's case. The Premier League refused to comment when approached by ESPN.

- Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained

No sanctions against City have been announced and sources at the Etihad Stadium have insisted that any guilty verdict will be met with an immediate appeal.

But with a number of Premier League executives now believing hundreds of rules breaches have been proven, sources have told ESPN that potential compensation claims from impacted clubs are being considered.

Sources have told ESPN that a number of clubs believe they have lost out on substantial revenue because of City's actions, including prize money, sponsorship bonuses and income generated by playing in European competitions.

City have maintained their innocence throughout the case with the Premier League and on Friday issued a statement insisting the process is "ongoing."

The club statement read: "The Premier League process remains ongoing with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence."

- Rodri 'believes in innocence' of Man City, says success 'deserved'

articles.headline: Barcelona's start to season is best in Europe's top 5 leagues for almost 100 years
articles.description: Barcelona have begun the season on fire, scoring 36 goals in their first eight matches. How does that compare to the best starts for all time? (Spoiler: Very well.)
articles.body:
LaLiga champions Barcelona have come flying out of the gate this season, with Hansi Flick's freewheeling side picking up where they left off last term and establishing themselves as perhaps the most in-form team on the planet.

Before their campaign was so rudely interrupted by a three-week international break, Barça won their first eight games of the season in all competitions, scoring 36 goals and conceding just eight. That run encompasses seven straight victories in LaLiga and a 5-1 thrashing of Feyenoord in their opening UEFA Champions League fixture.

Just to cement their absurd goal-scoring prowess, the Catalans have somehow managed to hit five goals or more on five separate occasions during those eight games. That is thanks in no small part to the incredible form of winger Raphinha, who has been excelling as a stand-in center forward after his club's summer pursuit of Atlético Madrid striker Julián Álvarez ended in failure.

- Soccer's wildest warmup kits: The good, the bad and the ugly

- Why this international break is longest ever (and that's a good thing)

- 2026 Ballon d'Or: Full men's, women's shortlists, host city, more

The nimble Brazil forward is already well clear at the top of the LaLiga goal-scoring charts with 12 goals from seven games (14 in eight across all competitions) so far. That prolific streak that culminated in back-to-back hat tricks last week, scored in the space of four days in resounding victories over Racing Santander and Sevilla.

After signing off with a "perfect" hat trick (i.e. left foot, right foot, header) against Sevilla, Raphinha can now claim to have made the best goal-scoring start to a season of any Barça player in history. The club captain narrowly pipped the previous record of 13 goals in eight games that was set by Cesar Rodríguez in 1948-49.

Indeed, Raphinha's early scoring form of 12 goals in the first eight LaLiga games of the season has only been bettered once in the 21st century. That was by Cristiano Ronaldo, who scored a frankly astounding 16 goals in eight games for Real Madrid at the start of the 2014-15 season.

Raphinha -- who has somehow missed out on being nominated for the Ballon d'Or -- isn't the only Barça player putting up ridiculous numbers this season. The rejuvenated Lamine Yamal has scored eight goals in as many games while laying on an additional six assists across all competitions -- becoming the youngest player in LaLiga history on record to reach (and subsequently surpass) the 50-assist mark in the process.

In short, things are going well right now at Camp Nou.

Barcelona's performances over the opening eight games of the season have given them a hefty early goal difference of plus-28. It certainly looks highly impressive on paper, but how does Barça's flying start to the campaign compare with the best starts ever made across the top strata of European football?

articles.headline: The unshakable bond between Aaron Glenn and Dan Campbell
articles.description: Aaron Glenn and Dan Campbell grew up playing and then coaching in the NFL. When Campbell made Glenn his DC, their bond was sealed.
articles.body:
The 2005 Dallas Cowboys were an incubator for future NFL head coaches, with six assistants from Bill Parcells' staff and two players from his roster ascending to the highest level of the football coaching profession.

The future coaches included an intense, long-in-the-tooth cornerback who played bigger than his 5-foot-9 frame and a hulking tight end who was biting kneecaps long before he spoke it into the NFL lexicon.

"He was the guy that Bill Parcells used to use to piss somebody off, and there were a number of fights in practice because of him," Aaron Glenn, the corner, said of Dan Campbell, the tight end.

Campbell and Glenn formed a strong bond that season together. They went from teammates in Dallas to assistant coaches with the New Orleans Saints to head coach-defensive coordinator with the Detroit Lions, enduring tough times and moments of sheer joy.

Their relationship was built on a promise by Campbell, who vowed to Glenn that he'd be his defensive coordinator if he ever became a head coach. Campbell did so in 2021 when he took over in Detroit, where the two developed an even closer bond, and doubled down in their first year together, standing by his guy in the 2022 season when it would have been easy to fire him after a rough start.

"One of the greatest days of my life was him getting the [New York Jets] job, and one of the worst days of my life was him getting that job because you know you're losing a little piece of you," Campbell said Friday. "That's what he meant to me and to us. So, that's hard."

On Sunday, they will face each other for the first time as head coaches (both sitting at 1-1), with Glenn bringing the Jets to Ford Field -- his home from 2021 to 2024. And nearly 500 miles away, at his house in Saratoga Springs, New York, the legendary Parcells will watch with pride.

"I always told them all that [coaching] is not for well-adjusted people, so I don't know why they would pick that profession," Parcells said with a hint of sarcasm, alluding to Campbell, Glenn and his many protégés. "But they're football guys. They love it. That's their game."

No change for the better

Campbell knew changes needed to be made in 2022 when the Lions were off to a 1-6 start.

Coming off a 32-27 loss to the Miami Dolphins, Detroit scored on all five of its first-half possessions and entered halftime with a comfortable 10-point lead. But Glenn's defense squandered it, leading to a fifth consecutive loss.

To that point, Glenn's unit was allowing a league-high 32.1 points per game, causing him to face heavy criticism, including calls for the first-time defensive coordinator to be fired.

But Campbell maintained faith in Glenn. And the defense gradually improved, which was instrumental in Detroit winning eight of its final 10 games where it allowed just 20.2 points per game throughout that stretch and narrowly missed the playoffs.

articles.headline: Giants' offense about to 'shift' with Jameis Winston
articles.description: The Giants' offense was starting to take shape with Dart as QB, but now Winston has to take over for the rest of the season.
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- It was several weeks into training camp for the New York Giants when offensive coordinator Matt Nagy mentioned that only half the team's plays were installed. At the time it seemed disconcerting, but it makes sense considering the Giants eventually practiced and installed close to 300 plays, according to offensive lineman Jon Runyan.

All that extensive work is poised to pay off. The offense greenlit by new coach John Harbaugh isn't only Jaxson Dart-specific. 

"Probably the biggest thing is -- one of the things with this offense when we first got started is we wanted to be able to be prepared to have multiple styles of offense," Nagy said. "And so, if something like this does happen, it doesn't put you in a hole where it changes everything."

The Giants' offense was starting to take shape with Dart as the quarterback before he suffered a knee injury in Week 2 and was placed on IR. His legs and ability to run were a big part of the run game. He had 54 yards in an impressive season-opening win over the Dallas Cowboys.

Backup QB Jameis Winston had two rushes for one yard in a Week 2 loss to the Los Angeles Rams and that came trying to escape a sack.

"All those plays are plays that we have, that we've been practicing and running, it's just kind of more like a shift maybe over a little bit as opposed to ... maybe a lane change as opposed to changing direction or anything like that," Harbaugh said. "More of a lane change."

The most notable change with Winston at quarterback will be the lack of QB runs. Winston, 32, isn't anywhere near the same threat as a runner as Dart.

The run-pass options are unlikely to be as big a piece of the Giants' offense.

"We did have a lot more Jaxson-driven-type quarterback runs," Runyan said. "It wasn't necessarily something that we were going to major in like we kind of did last year most of the time. So, unfortunately, a lot of that is out. I mean, could be here and there.

"Jameis is a gunslinger, obviously. So we're going to run our offense from a run point how I expect we have been through those two games. From a [quarterback] standpoint, I mean a little bit different. I don't think he's going to get the option to run a lot, but you never know."

Harbaugh has insisted since he arrived that the Giants are going to be a big, physical team. That is what they want to be. They are expected to continue to establish the power run game, try to make it effective and then take shots downfield.

This is where it could work with Winston.

"Well, he can throw it," Harbaugh said. "I mean, he's a big, strong, passing quarterback. He can throw the ball. Everybody that follows football has certainly seen Jameis play, and his strengths are evident. So that's what you build around."

articles.headline: 'Growing pains': What's going on with the Chargers' offense?
articles.description: Is the Chargers' offense too complicated for the team? What's going wrong with McDaniels' scheme in L.A.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Quarterback Justin Herbert furiously slammed his hands on the SoFi Stadium turf. He yelled as he stood up. Yelled as he began walking. Turned around and yelled some more. In the background, wide receiver Tre' Harris lay with his head buried in the turf.

Just a moment before, the Chargers failed to convert on third down in the third quarter of their Week 2 loss to the Raiders, with the play failing basically before it even started. Harris came in motion as the play clock wound down on third-and-inches with Herbert in the shotgun, but as center Jake Slaughter snapped the ball, it hit Harris in the leg.

Herbert jumped on the ball, and what followed was as intense of an outburst as he has had during a game in his seven-year career.

The moment was a microcosm for the Chargers' 2026 season through two weeks: an offense seemingly too complicated for this team and a quarterback who appears as frustrated as he ever has been in a season that's trending toward being another year where success remains a hypothetical. The offense will look to bounce back this Sunday against the Buffalo Bills (1 p.m. ET, Fox).

"Growing pains," coach Jim Harbaugh said. "Yeah, we got some growing pains."

"We're not standing on business in the least," offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel said.

McDaniel was the proverbial crown jewel of the Chargers' offseason.

After two seasons of middling offensive play, Harbaugh fired Greg Roman, the only offensive coordinator he had worked with in two stints in the NFL, following the Chargers' 16-3 wild-card round loss to the New England Patriots.

Fired in January after four seasons as the coach of the Miami Dolphins, McDaniel was still widely considered the top candidate available after the season. He's one of the most respected offensive minds in the NFL and chose to join the Chargers for the chance to work with Herbert and learn from Harbaugh.

General manager Joe Hortiz spent the offseason retooling the team's offense to suit McDaniel's vision, which needed a different type of player for his wide zone scheme.

McDaniel put up "wanted" posters for players he deemed essential, running back Keaton Mitchell and fullback Alec Ingold among them; Hortiz signed both. He added right guard Cole Strange, who worked with McDaniel when he coached the Dolphins, and drafted speedy wide receiver Brenen Thompson, partly at McDaniel's request.

Players and coaches were equally excited about the offense's potential in the offseason. McDaniel promised "career highs across the board" for all the wide receivers.

Instead, the Chargers had six fumbles versus the Raiders. Offensive tackle Joe Alt had three false starts. And Herbert didn't complete a pass of 20 air yards.

"I think I can just plain and simply say that it's below our expectations," McDaniel said. "I know it's below a lot of people's expectations as well."

articles.headline: How has Nakobe Dean reshaped the Raiders' defense?
articles.description: Nakobe Dean has stepped up in a big way to lead the Raiders' defense through two weeks.
articles.body:
HENDERSON, Nev. -- Nakobe Dean's impact on the Las Vegas Raiders' defense could be summarized by one play in the Week 2 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.

The Raiders led 17-14 in the fourth quarter and needed to stop the Chargers from converting on third-and-2 from the 28-yard line. Quarterback Justin Herbert handed the ball off to second-year running back Omarion Hampton, hoping he could convert the short-yardage situation. Dean had a different plan.

Dean maneuvered from the B-gap to the A-gap and met Hampton face-to-face before tackling him for no gain, forcing the Chargers to punt.

Dean's performances through his first two weeks with the Raiders have been filled with clutch moments. He has made plays all over the field, racking up 15 tackles, 1.5 sacks, four pressures and a pair of forced fumbles.

Over the offseason, the Raiders signed Dean to a three-year, $36 million deal. So far, it was money well spent.

"He's been the glue to our defense," safety Jeremy Chinn told ESPN. "It's crazy how much a linebacker in the middle of the field can make such a difference in the back end and front end."

Dean came to Las Vegas after four injury-riddled seasons with the Philadelphia Eagles, who selected him in the third round of the 2022 draft. Dean played in at least 15 games only twice with the Eagles. But when he was on the field, Dean was effective. He compiled 226 tackles, 7.5 sacks, three forced fumbles and 19 tackles for loss in 47 games (27 starts).

Las Vegas might have to give credit to Dean's intuition for landing one of the top off-ball linebackers in free agency. After the 2025 season, Dean had a competitive offer from the Dallas Cowboys along with the Raiders.

However, Dean thought about and prayed on both offers and ultimately, he couldn't go against his gut, which told him Las Vegas was the right fit.

Dean and fellow teammate Quay Walker have reshaped the Raiders' inside linebacker room. Last year, Las Vegas filled the room with veterans who were past their prime and signed to one-year deals. The production was inconsistent.

The Raiders took a new approach with Dean and Walker, both of whom are in the prime of their respective careers. And even though defensive coordinator Rob Leonard has had a strong start as a playcaller, Dean and Walker have been vital for the unit's ability to operate efficiently.

Dean, in particular, has added much-needed support in the passing game. In six pass-rush snaps, Dean recorded a pressure rate of 66.7% and three quarterback hits. He recorded three pressures against the Chargers.

As a whole, the Raiders have a league-leading sack total (eight) while ranked fifth in pressures (41) and first in pressure rate (50%). Of course, edge rusher Maxx Crosby has played a major role, but Dean has been much-needed support. Similar to Walker, Dean can line up in multiple spots up front. He has played 71 defensive snaps at inside linebacker, 12 at defensive tackle and 16 at outside linebacker.

articles.headline: What to expect from the much-anticipated Giants-Daboll reunion
articles.description: All eyes will be on former Giants coach Brian Daboll, who returns to New York as the Titans' offensive coordinator.
articles.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- There will be a lot of familiar faces in new places when the Tennessee Titans and New York Giants face off at MetLife Stadium on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, CBS).

All eyes will be on former Giants head coach Brian Daboll, who returns to New York as the Titans' offensive coordinator. Former Giants assistant coaches Shea Tierney and Carmen Bricillo, along with players Wan'Dale Robinson, Austin Schlottmann, Daniel Bellinger and Cor'Dale Flott, will also make the return to their former team's field. Waiting for Tennessee will be Giants quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan, who was the Titans' head coach before Robert Saleh was hired, and former Titans, now Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson. Although there will be so much familiarity scheme-wise, the Titans believe the deciding factor will be the players' execution.

"It really comes down to the Jimmys and Joes," Robinson told ESPN. "You don't really worry about the X's and the O's so much, it's more about the matchups and who you know you can go after, and I'm sure on their side, they're doing the same thing."

Daboll said he's grateful for the Giants giving him his first opportunity to be a head coach in 2022. He spent just over three seasons there, leading the Giants to a 20-40-1 record, including a divisional playoff game appearance in his first season. The Giants fired Daboll in November 2025 after a 2-8 record. But Daboll said there are no hard feelings and he's treating this like any other game as he prepares to return to MetLife Stadium.

"It's a one-week season every week, so you got to put everything you got into it," Daboll said Thursday. "That's what it is every week in the National Football League. I have a ton of respect for the people in that organization. From top down to the bottom, really good people in that building. I've been on a number of teams that played my former teams before. But it's about our players."

Robinson signed a four-year, $70 million deal to follow Daboll to Tennessee. Robinson echoed Daboll's sentiments, saying there's no bad blood between him and the Giants. Similar to Daboll, Robinson is excited to face his former team but insists it's "just another game at the end of the day."

The Titans' receivers should get opportunities to make plays against a Giants secondary decimated by injuries. Rookie cornerback Colton Hood was thrust into a starting role last week and allowed four completions on five targets for 42 yards and two touchdowns, primarily matching up with Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Davante Adams, a future Hall of Famer. Under Wilson, New York has resorted to man defense an NFL-high 18.8% of its snaps this season. Regardless of who's in the secondary, Saleh, who's very familiar with Wilson's defenses, is expecting a battle.

articles.headline: Former Manchester City chairman David Bernstein says financial punishment not 'sufficient' after Premier League breaches
articles.description: Former Manchester City chairman David Bernstein believes "money is not sufficient" in terms of a potential punishment for the club being found guilty on virtually all counts of breaching Premier League financial rules.
articles.body:
Former Manchester City chairman David Bernstein believes "money is not sufficient" in terms of a potential punishment for the club being found guilty on virtually all counts of breaching Premier League financial rules.

News broke on Friday that City had been found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges laid by the Premier League in February 2023, charges the club have always strenuously denied.

The charges date back to the 2009-10 season, since which time City have won multiple major trophies.

City are expected to appeal, and Bernstein, who was City chairman between 1998 and 2003, would want to see that process dealt with quickly.

He told Times Radio: "I felt absolutely awful, I felt in shock yesterday, actually. I think you've asked me on the programme because of my time as chair of City and the FA, but basically I'm a fan of Manchester City and have been a fan for 70 years.

"It's really awful that this great period of success, which followed many years of being less successful, when I was chair I think I helped get the club out of a very difficult period and started the road to better things.

"But to see all this tarnished in this way is very sad, I feel particularly bad for the wonderful supporters of the club who've stayed with the club through thick and thin. It's a pretty bad day I think for the fans in blue of Manchester."

Asked what the correct punishment would be, Bernstein said: "First of all, the timing of this I think is crucial. This whole process has taken too long already.

"So the appeal process now has to be done quickly because...you've got the club playing with this cloud over its head and it's just not viable.

"The appeal process cannot go on for year after year, I think that would be a disaster. Not just for this particular case but for English football generally. The timing is crucial.

"I can't give a view on the punishment. If they are found, after the appeal, guilty of 115 charges, my beloved club is going to face a very severe penalty.

"All I would say is that money is not sufficient, it would have to be something, unfortunately, more drastic than that."

Culture secretary Lisa Nandy described the case as "unsettling" for football fans and hopes for a swift resolution.

Speaking on BBC Radio Five Live, she said: "I think most football fans will be feeling this is not a good moment for football as a whole and I think Manchester City fans will be feeling very anxious about what happens next.

"You'll know this is a really longstanding investigation, it dates all the way back to allegations that begin in 2009. There is still a way to go with the investigation, Manchester City is contesting the charges.

"The football fans need to know the rules are applied fairly and consistently, they need to know they're upheld and they need to know the right decision has been reached.

"We do have a way to go with this, it's very unsettling for football fans and I hope that it can be resolved as swiftly as possible."

- Source

articles.headline: Who is Liverpool's new sporting director Julian Ward and what does he need to do?
articles.description: Julian Ward has been appointed as Liverpool's sporting director and he'll need to decide the futures of Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker, as well as targeting new faces.
articles.body:
And so yet another new Liverpool era begins. It has been a seismic few years at Anfield -- both on the pitch and off it -- with the drastic overhaul of the playing squad mirrored by a significant changing of the guard behind the scenes.

The latest of those changes comes with the appointment of Julian Ward as sporting director, following the departure of Richard Hughes earlier this month after just two years at the helm. Hughes informed the Liverpool hierarchy of his decision to leave the club earlier this year and has now taken up a new role at Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal.

The search for his successor was led by Mike Gordon, the president of club owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) -- by whom Ward was already employed as technical director. Even before he assumed that role in 2024, Ward was known to Liverpool supporters, having previously worked as the Reds' sporting director for the duration of the 2022-23 campaign.

However, with the landscape at Liverpool having changed markedly in the intervening years, how much of a challenge is Ward facing the second time around? And, in a period of such extreme transition, why is it imperative that he gets things right?

Who is he?

Ward's association with Liverpool dates back to 2012, when he joined from Manchester City to oversee the club's scouting network in Spain and Portugal. Over the next decade, he went on to assume a number of roles in the Reds' football operations department, including loan pathways and football partnerships manager and assistant sporting director to the vaunted Michael Edwards, who was at Liverpool in many roles behind the scenes from 2011-2022 (including a six-year stint as sporting director) and then was CEO of FSG from 2024-2026.

In 2022, after two years as Edwards' deputy, Ward replaced his superior as sporting director, although he only held the position for one season before departing for personal reasons in the summer of 2023. Alongside Edwards, he returned to the FSG fold in 2024, working as technical director as the organization sought to add a second club to its portfolio.

Those plans were officially shelved earlier this year, leading to Edwards' departure in June and subsequently the exit of Hughes following the conclusion of the summer's transfer window.

Born on Merseyside, Ward studied sports science at Liverpool John Moores University and enjoyed his first big break as part of Portugal boss Carlos Queiroz's technical team in 2008. He joined Manchester City in November 2010, with his work as the club's South American scouting strategist coinciding with their first Premier League title triumph in 2012.

Fluent in Portuguese, Ward's relationships in the country -- and in South America -- are viewed as an important asset.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal, Liverpool eye winger Kevin Schade
articles.description: Arsenal and Liverpool are upping their interest in Brentford's Kevin Schade, while the rest of Europe chases center backs. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Arsenal and Liverpool have identified Brentford's Kevin Schade as a potential addition to their squads, while the rest of Europe chases new center back options.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- There is increasing interest in Brentford winger Kevin Schade from Arsenal and Liverpool, according to Sky Sports. Brentford have held initial talks with the Germany international about extending his contract to see off that interest, with the aforementioned pair being the most serious about signing the 24-year-old when the summer transfer window drew to a close, although Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur are also admirers. Schade has entered the last two years of his current deal and Brentford are keen to offer him improved terms.

- Inter Milan center back Alessandro Bastoni has re-emerged as a transfer option for Barcelona, while Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester City also retain an interest in him, according to TEAMtalk. The 27-year-old was the topic of serious interest during the summer, but Inter remained firm on their valuation of close to £70 million for the Italy international. Chelsea would benefit from his ability to play in a back three, while Liverpool and City are looking at him as they prepare to eventually lose Virgil van Dijk and Rúben Dias.

- Liverpool, Chelsea and Manchester City are all keen on a potential deal for versatile Atlético Madrid midfielder Marcos Llorente, whose contract expires in the summer, according to TEAMtalk. Madrid are in talks with the 31-year-old over fresh terms and there is confidence within the Spanish club that an agreement will be reached. The situation has still attracted interest from the Premier League, with the trio of giants assessing whether Llorente could become available.

- Real Madrid are keeping an eye on Stuttgart center back Finn Jeltsch, reports Spanish newspaper AS. Madrid have signed Dean Huijsen and Ibrahima Konaté in the last two summer transfer windows but continue their efforts to strengthen the heart of their defence, and they are now monitoring several players from around the world. Jeltsch, 20, received his first Germany call-up from Jürgen Klopp this international window having joined Stuttgart from Nurnberg in January 2025.

- Liverpool are very satisfied with Ronald Araújo during his loan from Barcelona and could trigger their option to permanently sign the defender for €55 million, reports Spanish outlet Mundo Deportivo. The Uruguay international has played seven matches for the Reds, five of those coming as a starter, but he is already convincing the club and Andoni Iraola. The versatility displayed by the 27-year-old to play both right-back and centre-back has also caught the eye.

articles.headline: José Mourinho on 'non-negotiable' rules for Real Madrid to follow: 'Don't betray me'
articles.description: José Mourinho has spoken about his managerial philosophy, warning of the importance of trust between players and coach -- and "non-negotiable" rules for his squad to follow -- as he looks to build a new winning team at Real Madrid.
articles.headlineJa: ジョゼ・モウリーニョ、レアル・マドリードが守るべき「譲れない」ルールについて語る：「私を裏切るな」
articles.descriptionJa: ジョゼ・モウリーニョはレアル・マドリードで新たな常勝チームを築こうとする中、自身の監督哲学を語り、選手と監督の間の信頼関係の重要性、そしてチームが守るべき「譲れない」ルールについて警告しました。
